label: Robots.txt allows the search and AI retrieval crawlers
claim: A crawler disallowed at the root never sees the page — every later optimization is worth zero for that engine until robots.txt is fixed. Blocking a retrieval crawler removes the site from the corresponding answer engine's source pool.

evidence.finding: Of 411 parsable robots.txt files in the top 500: 81 hard-block GPTBot, 43 block OAI-SearchBot, 62 block PerplexityBot, 84 block ClaudeBot — while Googlebot is hard-blocked by only 4.
evidence.effect: ~10% of top-500 block at least one AI retrieval crawler at the root

evidence.finding: GPTBot is blocked by 14.3% of the top 10,000 sites; top-1k sites block ~1.5× more often than ranks 5k–10k.
robots.txt changes take effect in ChatGPT search in about 24 hours.

notes: Blocking Googlebot is rare on the top 500 (4/411) — the entire negotiation is about AI crawlers, and it is a policy choice with visibility consequences.

label: Three crawler classes are three separate decisions
claim: Training crawlers (GPTBot, CCBot, Google-Extended token), search/answer-index crawlers (OAI-SearchBot, PerplexityBot, Claude-SearchBot), and user-fetching agents (ChatGPT-User, Perplexity-User, Claude-User) require separate robots.txt policies. Blocking one does not block the others.

evidence.finding: OpenAI operates GPTBot (training), OAI-SearchBot (search index), and ChatGPT-User (live user fetch) as separate agents.
Perplexity-User fetches in real time for a user query and generally ignores robots.txt; PerplexityBot is the separate indexing crawler.
Google-Extended is a token controlling Gemini training/grounding, not a crawler and not a Search/AIO opt-out.
92.3% of top news sites that blocked Google-Extended were still cited in AI answers.

notes: The cheapest GEO win is usually policy: allow the retrieval crawlers, treat training as a separate choice, and never assume Google-Extended controls AI Overviews.

label: Accurate sitemap with honest lastmod
claim: A sitemap containing only canonical 200-status URLs with truthful lastmod dates accelerates discovery and re-crawl — Perplexity explicitly treats sitemap freshness as a recrawl signal.

evidence.finding: New pages submitted with correct lastmod saw first AI-crawler fetches within 14 minutes (GPTBot) and 43% coverage across all major crawlers within 24 hours.
Perplexity uses sitemap lastmod as a recrawl signal and slows for stale dates and erroring pages.

label: Bing index pipeline live (BWT + IndexNow)
claim: Bing's index supplies a large share of ChatGPT's and all of Copilot's candidate pool, so Bing Webmaster Tools hygiene and IndexNow pings are AI-search infrastructure, not an afterthought.

evidence.finding: 87% of sources cited by ChatGPT Search appeared in Bing's top 20 for the same query — vs 56% overlap with Google's top 20.
Microsoft says IndexNow notifications reduce stale URL references in Copilot grounding results; BWT now reports AI citation share.

label: Pages are indexed and snippet-eligible
claim: A page must be indexed and eligible to appear with a snippet before any search or AI surface can use it; unexpected noindex, canonical chains, and error status codes zero everything downstream.

evidence.finding: Google states AI features are grounded in core Search ranking — indexable, snippet-eligible pages are the prerequisite.

notes: Practitioner standard; the audit engine already enforces it. Gate semantics: content work on a noindexed page is worth $0 and the report should say so.

label: Unique title, H1, and meta description matched to intent
claim: One clear H1 stating the value proposition, a unique descriptive title, and a persuasive meta description are table stakes for both ranked lists and extraction.

evidence.finding: On-page contract: one title formula per template, one H1 stating the value proposition, meta ~150–160 chars with a concrete next step.

notes: Practitioner standard. Quantified effect sizes vary by study; title rewrites show up mainly in CTR, not ranking correlation.

label: Topic coverage that absorbs query fan-out
claim: One question fans out into several parallel sub-queries before an AI answer is written; pages that already answer the natural follow-up questions get cited for sub-intents the original query never mentioned.

evidence.finding: Google describes query fan-out as core to AI Overviews and AI Mode, and warns that manufacturing pages per fan-out variant is scaled-content abuse.
37.1% of AI Overview-cited URLs rank in the organic top 10; 26.2% rank 11–100 and 36.7% are outside the top 100 (863K keywords; 4M AIO URLs). The same metric read ~76% in mid-2025.
Fan-out rankings predict AIO citation at Spearman 0.77; pages ranking the main query plus at least one fan-out are 161% more likely to be cited.
AI Mode shows only ~12% strict top-10 overlap — 88% of cited URLs are not in the SERP top 10.
50% of domains cited in AI Overviews were absent from the organic top 10 across 645 queries.

notes: Breadth-within-a-topic on one strong page beats thin pages per query variant.

label: Entity-rich copy (names, not pronouns)
claim: Passages that keep entity names, numbers, and dates explicit survive retrieval chunking; pronouns and 'as mentioned above' do not.

evidence.finding: RAG systems retrieve at passage level (~256–512 token chunks) and each section should be self-contained and quotable.

notes: Mechanism is well-established (passage retrieval); direct citation-effect studies are thin.

label: Internal links with descriptive anchors, hub → cluster
claim: Each page links to 2–4 relevant pages with descriptive anchors; pillar pages link out to the cluster. Discovery compounds and machine readers get the relationship graph.

evidence.finding: Internal-link contract: money pages first, descriptive anchors, hub pages link out to the whole set.

label: Link authority (referring domains, quality)
claim: Links remain one of the strongest documented correlates of ranking; for AI answers they also feed the retrieval-side source quality signals.

evidence.finding: Link metrics correlate with AI Overview brand mentions more weakly than brand signals do (DR 0.326, referring domains 0.295, backlinks 0.218 vs branded web mentions 0.664).
Compiled research treats links as a core authority layer; mass guest posting has diminishing returns and inauthentic mentions are spam-risk.

notes: Classic-SEO side of link authority: awaiting the 2025–26 ranking-factor correlation studies (stage-3 research stream). For AI answers specifically, links are already visible as a weaker correlate than brand mentions.

label: Brand mentions and consistent naming across the web
claim: Unlinked mentions, community discussion, and consistent brand spelling feed the entity layer models use to resolve 'who is this' — NAP-style consistency everywhere.

evidence.finding: Entity resolution: consistent naming + sameAs chains + Wikidata presence make the brand a 'known thing' rather than unresolved text; vendor claims of 3× citation lifts are unverified but the mechanism is well-established.

Across 75K brands, AI Overview brand mentions correlated most with branded web mentions (Spearman 0.664), branded anchors (0.527), and branded search volume (0.392) — league above link metrics. Top web-mention quartile averaged 169 AIO mentions vs 14 for the next quartile; 26% of brands had zero. Seer: ChatGPT brand mentions correlate with Google keyword visibility 0.65 vs backlinks 0.10.

label: Original data studies as citation magnets
claim: Original statistics are the single most durable citation asset: the strongest measured GEO lever is adding quantitative data, and every stat others quote links back.

evidence.finding: Statistics addition lifted visibility +31% relative on position-adjusted word count — the second-strongest lever after quotations.
A 'State of AI Indexation' study is the highest-leverage content program that isn't a money page; the dataset is the citation magnet.

label: Core Web Vitals within budget (LCP ≤ 2.5s, INP ≤ 200ms, CLS ≤ 0.1 at p75)
claim: Field CWV at p75 are a documented (if modest) ranking input and a UX gate; static HTML, explicit dimensions, and transform/opacity-only motion protect the budget.

evidence.finding: Google's thresholds: LCP ≤ 2.5s, INP ≤ 200ms, CLS ≤ 0.1 at the 75th percentile.
Field data for 18M+ origins makes CWV measurable per origin without lab runs.

notes: Ranking effect is real but small relative to gates above; the bigger risk is CLS-destroying motion and JS-gated above-fold content.

label: No bot wall in front of AI crawlers
claim: robots.txt can say yes while the server says no: WAF/CDN bot rules, anti-bot flows, and challenge pages return 403s or empty shells to non-browser clients — the site is invited but barricaded.

evidence.finding: 130 of 500 top sites (26%) returned a wall or empty shell to a non-browser client; 100 of those have robots.txt open to every AI retrieval crawler — invited, then barricaded.
25% of 405 small-business sites had answer-critical elements visible in a browser but absent from raw HTML; sites on server-rendering platforms were AI-invisible 4% of the time vs 28.3% otherwise.

notes: Test with curl -A "GPTBot" … | grep, not DevTools. Cloudflare and similar WAFs can block silently even when robots.txt allows.

label: Main content ships in server-rendered HTML
claim: Most AI crawlers do not execute JavaScript. Content that only appears after client-side rendering is invisible to ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, and Copilot — only Google's surfaces render JS, and late.

evidence.finding: None of the major AI crawlers (GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, Bytespider) execute JavaScript across 500M+ fetches.
Among 324 readable homepages, the median keeps 71.4% of browser-visible content in raw HTML (p25 48.8%, p75 93.0%). 35% of the top 500 are unreadable or unreachable to a non-rendering client.
A controlled test had ChatGPT report it 'could not read the content because it relied on JavaScript' — then read the identical content after server-rendering.

notes: The single largest technical gate for AI visibility — and the axis our top-500 study owns.

label: Headings arrive in raw HTML
claim: Pages whose headings ship in raw HTML are the pages whose content ships too — the strongest same-page signal we measure.

evidence.finding: Heading coverage and content coverage correlate at r = 0.647 across 300 readable homepages — the strongest same-page relationship in the study (stronger than JSON-LD presence at r = 0.15).

notes: Dynamic headlines (Apple 14.5% heading coverage, Guardian 20.7%) are common and fixable: render headings server-side.

label: JSON-LD present in raw HTML (not injected client-side)
claim: Structured data is an independent layer — it does not lift citations by itself, but server-rendered schema is required for rich results and entity clarity; tag-manager-injected schema is invisible to non-rendering crawlers.

evidence.finding: Of 324 readable homepages, 170 (52.5%) ship JSON-LD server-side, 12 declare it client-only, 142 declare none. JSON-LD presence barely correlates with content coverage (r = 0.15).
Controlled test across 1,885 pages: schema markup produced no measurable AI-citation uplift (within noise).

notes: Keep schema for rich results + entity clarity; don't sell it as a citation lever. The schema story on top sites is healthier than the content story (most schema is server-rendered).

label: Critical facts (prices, specs) exist as text, not images
claim: Screenshots and images are invisible to AI crawlers; pricing pages that bury the number in a screenshot cannot be quoted when engines are asked 'how much does X cost?'.

evidence.finding: Pricing pages are extraction targets; screenshots are invisible to AI crawlers — put the real numbers in text with an answer sentence up top.

label: Definition-first opening (2–3 quotable sentences)
claim: The first substantive paragraph should answer 'what is this?' with the entity named — it is the passage AI engines quote, and fluency is one of the strongest measured levers.

evidence.finding: Fluency optimization lifted visibility +28% relative; the best combination was fluency + statistics.
Check X1: answer-first opening with entity nouns, no windup — the format engines extract.
Definition markers were associated with +57% citation influence across 23,745 citation-level feature rows (descriptive, not causal).

label: Each section opens with a complete, standalone answer
claim: Retrieval happens at passage level: a standalone passage that fully answers a sub-query is what gets retrieved. Answer-first, then detail — this beats a slow build to the point.

evidence.finding: RAG indexes split pages into ~256–512-token passages and retrieve at passage level; one idea per section, question-shaped headings, explicit entities.
Fan-out + RAG over the Search index select passages across sub-queries; Google debunks 'special chunking' but the passage-level mechanism stands.

label: Comparison tables for 'X vs Y' and 'best of' queries
claim: Tables are the extraction format engines prefer for comparison queries — every money page should carry at least one structured artifact (table, numbered steps, or checklist) matched to intent.

evidence.finding: Format matching: tables for comparisons, numbered steps for how-tos, bullet lists for options — AI engines preferentially extract structured artifacts.
Comparison content scored +55% citation influence (descriptive); comparison questions carry the highest mean citation influence of any question type.
Structured HTML yielded 2.6× citation rates and 4.0× extraction fidelity in a controlled setup (ACM Hypertext 2026).

notes: Mechanism is plausible and practitioner-standard; direct controlled evidence is limited.

label: FAQ block whose text matches its schema byte-for-byte
claim: A short FAQ (3–6 real questions) with concise standalone answers is cheap extractable content; schema must match the visible text exactly per Google policy.

evidence.finding: Check X4: FAQ block with FAQPage schema matching visible text — enforced internally by check:seo parity rule.
Google requires markup to match visible content and states no special schema is needed for AI features.
Q&A surface format scored −5.7% citation influence (descriptive) — an FAQ block is not itself a citation lever; the standalone answers are.
FAQ blocks' apparent citation effects collapsed under domain fixed effects (Simpson's paradox) — treat FAQ as extraction hygiene, not a proven lever.

label: Numeric explicitness — real prices, dates, units
claim: Engines prefer directness and specificity: 'contact us for pricing' is unquotable, while real numbers are the raw material for statistics-driven citations.

evidence.finding: Statistics addition lifted visibility +31%; specificity patterns follow the same mechanism.

label: Single-purpose pages over sprawling ones
claim: Perplexity rewards direct answers in the first ~100 words and single-purpose pages; sprawling multi-topic pages dilute the passage that gets retrieved.

evidence.finding: Engine mechanics: Perplexity fetches ~10 pages, cites 3–8; rewards first-100-word answers and single-purpose pages; recency can out-cite authority.

label: No thin or near-duplicate template pages
claim: Programmatic pages need ≥300 unique words or they are merged/noindexed; near-duplicate template variants trip scaled-content-abuse lines in both Search and AI surfaces.

evidence.finding: Programmatic guardrails: ≥300 unique words per page or noindex/merge; unique title+meta per page; never generate pages purely for fan-out variants.
Manufacturing content for every fan-out query variant violates the scaled-content-abuse policy.
Word count correlates ~zero with citation position (Spearman 0.04); 53.4% of citations point to pages under 1,000 words. Thin means low-value, not short.

label: Attributed quotations from named people
claim: Quotation addition was the single strongest measured GEO tactic — real quotes with attribution, not adjectives.

evidence.finding: Quotation addition: visibility index 27.2 vs 19.3 baseline — +41% relative, the best single method across 10,000 queries; reproduced live on Perplexity.

notes: Matters most for people/society/history topics per the study's domain notes.

label: Quantitative data with real numbers
claim: Adding statistics is the second-strongest lever and the best pairing with fluency; numbers beat adjectives everywhere.

evidence.finding: Statistics addition: +31% relative visibility; best combo fluency + statistics.
Pages with numbers/statistics scored +62% citation influence in the open feature dataset (descriptive).

notes: Matters most for law/gov/opinion-style content per the study's domain notes.

label: Outbound citations to credible sources
claim: Citing credible sources lifts visibility up to +28% — and it is the biggest lever for lower-ranked sites, while top-ranked sites can even lose ground from it.

evidence.finding: Cite-sources: +28% average; +115% lift for a rank-5 site, −30% for a rank-1 site; matters most for factual content.

label: Fluency — clear, readable prose
claim: Fluency optimization compounds with everything (+28% alone, best combined with statistics). Writing clearly for humans is the tactic; anti-human keyword-speak hurts.

evidence.finding: Fluency optimization: +28% relative visibility; compounds with statistics.

label: No keyword stuffing (−8% — the only negative lever)
claim: Keyword stuffing was the only tactic that reduced visibility in the foundational study — chasing keywords is actively counterproductive for AI answers.

evidence.finding: Keyword stuffing: visibility index 17.7 vs 19.3 baseline — −8%, the only negative method measured.

label: Domain-appropriate technical terms (mild lift)
claim: Adding technical terms measured a mild +18% — real vocabulary from the field beats generic marketing language, but it is far weaker than quotes and statistics.

evidence.finding: Technical terms: +18% relative visibility; easy-to-understand +14%; authoritative tone +10%; unique words +6%.

label: Organization schema with @id, logo, sameAs chain
claim: A complete Organization node — @id, name, url, logo, foundingDate, sameAs[] to authoritative profiles — is the self-declaration that anchors entity resolution.

evidence.finding: Entity layer: Organization JSON-LD + sameAs chain to LinkedIn, X, GitHub, Crunchbase, G2, Product Hunt, and ideally a Wikidata Q-number make the brand a 'known thing'.
Organization/WebSite/SameAs vocabulary definitions.

notes: Mechanism (knowledge-graph grounding) is well-established; rigorous causal studies are thin — see outliers.

label: Wikidata entity + bidirectional link
claim: A Wikidata Q-number (P856 official website ↔ our sameAs) feeds Google's Knowledge Graph and most LLM training corpora — the cheapest durable 'I exist' signal.

evidence.finding: Wikidata's notability bar is 'verifiable existence' (far below Wikipedia's); one-time setup, durable payoff; bidirectional linking recommended.

label: Author bylines with credentials on editorial content
claim: Named authors with credentials (Person schema) are an E-E-A-T proxy that matters most in YMYL verticals; anonymous content competes worse for trust-sensitive answers.

evidence.finding: Search Quality Rater Guidelines define E-E-A-T and its per-topic importance, highest for YMYL.

label: Fresh, maintained pages (dateModified + visible last-updated)
claim: Freshness is a retrieval signal: most AI-cited pages were updated within a year, citation half-life runs ~39–68 days for timely queries, and Perplexity explicitly rewards recency.

evidence.finding: ~75% of AI-cited pages were updated within a year (Gemini 78%, ChatGPT 73%, Perplexity 65%); fitted citation half-life ≈39 days (timely) / 68 days otherwise; ~65% of cited sources churn day-to-day.
Perplexity recrawls established sites weekly-to-monthly; stale dateModified slows recrawl; a recent update can out-cite older, higher-authority content.
AI-cited pages average 1,064 days old vs 1,432 for organic results — engines cite fresher pages on average (16.975M URLs).

Median citation half-life measured at 11 days panel-relative (78% of cited pages fall to half-peak within 14 days); pages cited by 5+ engines persist 5.5× longer. Conflicts with the 39–68-day fitted estimate — definitional, see outliers.

label: Indexable, maintained changelog / update log
claim: A changelog is a frequently-accidentally-noindexed freshness surface; keeping it indexable gives engines evidence of a real maintenance cadence.

evidence.finding: Changelog: frequently noindexed by accident; keep indexable as a freshness signal.

label: Presence on the third-party sites engines cite
claim: Most AI citations point at third-party sources — Reddit, YouTube, Wikipedia, review platforms, listicles. A clean site alone is half the game; the other half is being discussed where engines look.

evidence.finding: In an 83,670-citation dataset, 82.9% of AI citations pointed to non-brand sites; brand sites earn 13.5% (ChatGPT) to 22.2% (Claude) of mentions.

Across 8 models and 11.84B citations, 57% of citations go to brand/company-owned sites (ChatGPT 47%, Gemini 69%) — a different cut: the 82.9% figure's denominator is mentions of the queried brand, Profound's is all cited domains.
84% of AI citations are earned media; journalism is 25–27% of citations; press releases 0.04%.

notes: Off-site is genuinely half of GEO — keep it an unscored checklist until prompt-run data exists.

label: Accurate G2 / Capterra / Product Hunt / Crunchbase listings
claim: Review platforms feed AI answers directly for commercial queries; accurate listings and real reviews are quotable third-party evidence about the brand.

evidence.finding: Priority off-site targets: G2/Capterra/Product Hunt profiles; they feed AI answers and are cited for commercial comparison queries.

label: Google Search Console opted into generative AI features
claim: The Generative AI performance report (AI Overviews / AI Mode impressions) requires opting the property into generative AI features — without it you are optimizing blind.

evidence.finding: Measurement lives in the GSC Generative AI performance report; opt-in required.

label: Bing Webmaster Tools AI Performance / Citation Share enabled
claim: BWT's AI Performance report tracks citations across Copilot and Bing AI summaries with Intent/Topic breakdowns — free ground truth for the Bing-fed engines.

evidence.finding: AI Performance report (Feb 2026; Citation Share + Compare added June 2026) — enable on day one.

label: A fixed 30–50 prompt buyer set tracked monthly across engines
claim: Track a fixed prompt set across ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini/AI Mode, Copilot, and Claude separately — engine source overlap is only ~14% and citations churn ~65% day-to-day, so single 'AI visibility scores' mislead.

evidence.finding: Only 14% of top-50 mentioned sources are shared across ChatGPT, Perplexity, and AI Overviews.
~65% of cited sources change from day to day — trendlines beat snapshots.

Across five engines, 79.6% of cited sources appear on only one engine and just 0.31% on all five; only 2.35–2.45% of ChatGPT/Perplexity/AIO citations are shared by all three (Growth Memo, 3.7M citations).
Mean pairwise cross-engine Jaccard 0.0079; same-engine URL turnover 67% within ~1 day.

label: GA4 AI-referrer channel group and crawler log checks
claim: AI referrals are small (~0.3% of traffic) but convert at multiples of organic — track chatgpt.com, perplexity.ai, copilot.microsoft.com, gemini.google.com referrers and watch server logs for 403/429s on Tier-1 crawlers.

evidence.finding: Perplexity referrals converted at 10.5% vs 1.76% Google organic on one B2B client; ChatGPT 15.9%.
AI-referred retail conversions +31% vs non-AI; revenue per visit +254% YoY.

notes: Traffic share ~0.3% (geo-research §10) — small but strategically tracked.

label: Local entity signals (GBP, NAP consistency, reviews)
claim: Local intent is resolved by engines through business-profile data and consistency signals — the map layer of SEO has its own rules that site content alone cannot substitute for.
notes: Practitioner standard for local verticals — awaiting quantified 2025–26 local-factor studies for evidence entries.

label: Format matched to query intent (lists for commercial, articles for informational)
claim: The winning format depends on intent: commercial queries send ~41% of citations to listicles; informational queries send ~46% to articles. Format advantages are unstable — ChatGPT listicle citations fell ~30% MoM in Jan 2026 — so build for extraction, not for a format fashion.

evidence.finding: 63% of AI citations across six engines went to listicles; 71–86% of cited listicles also ranked organically.
Commercial-intent queries: 40.86% of citations to listicles; informational: 45.5% to articles.
ChatGPT listicle citations dropped ~30% Dec 2025 → Jan 2026 while pages carrying fresh-year signals rose; structured/numbered formats survived.
Listicles + articles + product pages ≈ 52% of citations; intent decides which wins.

notes: Format is a factor, not a rule. Vendor share numbers use different denominators (mention share vs URL share vs citation share) — never sum or average them.

label: Clean semantic HTML (landmarks, real lists, heading hierarchy)
claim: Semantic, structured HTML improves extraction fidelity for both AI engines and agentic browsers; the strongest controlled evidence found 2.6× citation rates for structured markup.

evidence.finding: Structured HTML yielded 2.6× citation rates and 4.0× extraction fidelity (ACM Hypertext 2026).
Semantic HTML showed among the strongest citation associations in the GEO-16 framework across 1,702 citations.

notes: Also the layer agentic browsers read (a11y tree/DOM) — helps humans, crawlers, and agents at once.

label: Canonical URL present and self-consistent
claim: Every indexable page declares a single canonical URL that matches its (redirect-resolved) address, preventing duplicate-content dilution.

evidence.finding: Canonicalization is a core indexing signal; inconsistent or missing canonicals cause duplicate URLs to split ranking signals.
Only 29/59 (49%) of audited top sites' homepages exposed a canonical link in raw HTML; 30/59 did not.

notes: Raw-HTML check (AI crawlers don't execute JS to discover canonical).

label: Meta description within length budget and unique per page
claim: A 120-160 character, unique meta description improves SERP snippet control and gives AI engines a ready-made passage to quote.

evidence.finding: Meta descriptions are used for snippets; unique descriptions improve click-through and disambiguation.
Median meta-description length on audited top sites was ~126 chars; 21/59 (36%) had none or were empty in raw HTML.

label: Open Graph + Twitter Card tags for social/AI preview
claim: OG and Twitter Card metadata control how links render in social and chat surfaces, which increasingly feed AI answer engines' source previews.

evidence.finding: Semantic markup layers (HTML, ARIA, schema) each have distinct roles; social cards are the preview layer for citation surfaces.
OG title present on 38/59 (64%), OG description on 32/59 (54%), OG image on 28/59 (47%) in raw HTML.

label: HTML lang attribute and charset declared
claim: Declaring lang (and a UTF-8 charset) lets engines and AI systems identify language, apply correct tokenization, and avoid mojibake in extraction.

evidence.finding: Document language and encoding are baseline accessibility/i18n signals consumed by browsers, crawlers and assistive tech.
lang present on 45/59 (76%); charset declared on 56/59 (95%) in raw HTML.

label: Semantic landmark elements (main, nav, header, footer, article)
claim: Landmark elements let AI extractors and agentic browsers identify the main content region and discard navigation/boilerplate.

evidence.finding: Sites with >70% semantic compliance achieved 2.8x higher citation rates in Perplexity and Gemini for entity queries than sites with <30% compliance (Momentic 2026 analysis).
Using main/article/section instead of div containers lets crawlers delineate page hierarchy more clearly; 80%+ semantic markup indexes 25-40% quicker.
Only 25/59 (42%) exposed <main>, 23/59 (39%) <nav>, 21/59 (36%) <header>, 23/59 (39%) <footer> in raw HTML; rendered counts were higher (JS-injected landmarks).

notes: Distinct from geo.extract.semantic-html (general clean HTML); this factor is specifically about landmark regions that bound main content.

label: Single H1 and valid heading sequence (no skipped levels)
claim: A single H1 declaring the primary topic with a non-skipping H2/H3 outline makes passage chunking and answer extraction reliable.

evidence.finding: Top pages nearly always include target keywords in H1 tags for semantic hierarchy (SE Ranking).
Only 31/59 (53%) had exactly one H1 and 23/59 (39%) had a valid (non-skipping) heading sequence in raw HTML; rendered counts were similar or worse (30/57, 15/57).

notes: Heading coverage is noisy on dynamic pages; normalize before publishing (per docs/data-assets §6.2).

label: Descriptive alt text on content images
claim: Alt text is the only machine-readable description of images for non-vision systems; missing alt makes image content unquotable.

evidence.finding: Alt text is required for image accessibility and is consumed by crawlers and AI vision pipelines as the text fallback.
Raw HTML: 43/1207 images (3.6%) had no alt; rendered pass had 116/2205 (5.3%) missing alt (JS-injected images are worse).

label: Skip-to-main-content link present
claim: A skip link lets keyboard and agent users (and extractors) jump past repeated navigation to the main content.

evidence.finding: Skip links are a baseline accessibility pattern that also helps automated agents reach primary content faster.
Only 11/59 (19%) of audited top sites exposed a skip-to-main link in raw HTML.

label: JSON-LD matches visible page content (no schema spam)
claim: Structured data must describe the page that actually renders; schema that contradicts visible content is ignored or penalized.

evidence.finding: Controlled test of schema markup vs AI citations (May 2026).
Field test: if a property doesn't match visible content, remove it until it does; schema spam and conflicting signals are anti-patterns.
JSON-LD present on 19/59 (32%) raw and 21/57 (37%) rendered; types stable across passes where present, indicating mostly server-rendered schema.

notes: Extends geo.render.jsonld-raw (presence) with a parity/quality dimension.

label: Breadcrumbs in HTML plus BreadcrumbList schema
claim: Breadcrumbs expose site hierarchy to crawlers and give AI engines a machine-readable path from leaf page to category to home.

evidence.finding: Breadcrumbs help users and search engines understand page position in site hierarchy; BreadcrumbList schema enables rich results.
Only 1/59 audited top sites exposed a breadcrumb nav in raw HTML; tables were similarly rare (2/59) on homepages.

notes: Homepage-only sample; breadcrumb adoption is expected to be higher on deep pages. Audit should check representative money pages.

label: Important pages reachable within 3 clicks from home
claim: Keeping money pages within 3 hops of the homepage preserves crawl budget and ensures AI crawlers (which rarely paginate deep) can reach them.

evidence.finding: Click depth should be capped at 3 hops from the homepage to protect crawlability and PageRank flow.
Internal links are the roads crawlers use to discover pages; orphaned or deep pages are effectively invisible.

label: Hub-and-spoke topic clusters with a pillar page
claim: Grouping supporting pages around a pillar page concentrates topical authority and gives AI engines a coherent entity cluster to cite.

evidence.finding: Content clusters group a foundational pillar with supporting articles; the strongest internal links make sense to a reader.
Hub-and-spoke architecture is a 2026 internal-linking standard for establishing topical authority.

label: No orphan pages (every indexable page has >=1 internal link)
claim: Pages with zero internal inlinks are effectively unreachable for crawlers and AI agents, regardless of sitemap inclusion.

evidence.finding: A page with zero internal links is genuinely hard to find, for crawlers and humans alike.
Orphan page elimination is a documented 2026 internal-linking standard.

label: Clean, descriptive, hierarchical URLs
claim: Readable, hierarchical URLs (lowercase, hyphenated, no opaque IDs) improve crawl efficiency and serve as an entity signal in citations.

evidence.finding: Simple, descriptive URLs help users and search engines; avoid complex parameters where possible.

label: Persistent, crawlable primary navigation (real <a href>)
claim: Primary navigation must be server-rendered anchor links; JS-only or button-based nav is invisible to non-rendering crawlers.

evidence.finding: Google can generally crawl a link when it's a standard <a> element with an href; clickable elements that aren't coded as links break discovery.
Major AI crawlers execute zero JavaScript; navigation rendered only client-side is unreachable.

label: XML sitemap covers all indexable pages
claim: An XML sitemap listing every indexable URL (with lastmod) is the fallback discovery path when internal links miss pages.

evidence.finding: Sitemaps help search engines discover and prioritize URLs, especially on large or new sites.
Complements sitemap freshness (disc.sitemap-freshness) with a coverage dimension.
